title: Total media spend
context: The Weekly table (rows 2-79) has one row per channel per week. Finance wants the quarter's total ad spend.
task: How much did the team spend on advertising in total across every channel and week?
hint: Find the column holding weekly spend and total it.

title: Total attributed revenue
context: Marketing reports the revenue their campaigns brought in.
task: What is the total revenue attributed across all channels and weeks?
hint: One column holds the revenue for each week's row.

title: Overall ROAS
context: Return on ad spend is total revenue divided by total spend, shown to 2 decimals.
task: What was the overall return on ad spend for the quarter, rounded to 2 decimals?
hint: Divide total revenue by total spend, then round the result.

title: Click-through rate
context: CTR measures how many impressions turned into clicks.
task: What fraction of impressions became clicks for the week in row 2?
hint: Divide that row's clicks by its impressions.

title: Cost per click
context: Buyers watch what each click costs, to 2 decimals.
task: What did each click cost for the week in row 2, rounded to 2 decimals?
hint: Spend divided by clicks, then round.

title: Cost per acquisition
context: CPA is what it costs to win one conversion, to 2 decimals.
task: What did each conversion cost for the week in row 2, rounded to 2 decimals?
hint: Spend divided by conversions, then round.

title: Conversion rate
context: The dashboard shows what share of clicks convert, as a percentage.
task: What percentage of the clicks in row 2 converted? Show it formatted like 4.2%.
hint: Divide conversions by clicks and format the result as a percentage.

title: Google Search weeks
context: Each channel appears once per week in the Weekly table.
task: How many rows in the Weekly table belong to the Google Search channel?
hint: Count the channel column where it equals Google Search.

title: Performance-objective weeks
context: Every week's row carries an objective label.
task: How many weekly rows had an objective of Performance?
hint: Count the objective column where it equals Performance.

title: Big-spend weeks
context: Finance flags any channel-week that spent more than 5,000.
task: How many weekly rows had spend above 5,000?
hint: Count the spend column with a greater-than criterion.

title: Meta total spend
context: The Meta channel owner wants their slice of the budget.
task: How much was spent on the Meta channel in total?
hint: Sum spend, but only for rows where the channel is Meta.

title: Email conversions
context: Email is the cheapest channel; the team wants its total output.
task: How many conversions did the Email channel generate in total?
hint: Sum conversions where the channel is Email.

title: Brand-objective spend
context: Leadership wants to know how much went to brand-building.
task: How much was spent across all weeks whose objective was Brand?
hint: Sum spend, filtered to rows where the objective is Brand.

title: Average weekly spend
context: A KPI tile shows the typical channel-week spend to 2 decimals.
task: What is the average spend per weekly row, rounded to 2 decimals?
hint: Average the spend column, then round.

title: Typical LinkedIn week
context: How much does a typical LinkedIn week cost?
task: What is the average weekly spend on the LinkedIn channel?
hint: Average spend, filtered to LinkedIn rows.

title: Best revenue week
context: Which channel-week brought in the most money?
task: What is the highest revenue recorded in any single weekly row?
hint: Look for the maximum in the revenue column.

title: Cheapest click target
context: The Channels table lists each channel's target cost-per-click.
task: What is the lowest target CPC set for any channel?
hint: The Channels table has a target CPC column; find its minimum.

title: Profit or loss?
context: A week pays for itself when its revenue beats its spend.
task: Label the week in row 2 as "Profit" if its revenue exceeded its spend, otherwise "Loss".
hint: A single IF comparing the revenue and spend cells.

title: ROAS band
context: A week is Strong when its revenue is at least triple its spend.
task: Label the week in row 2 as "Strong" if its return on ad spend is 3 or more, otherwise "Weak".
hint: Test the revenue-to-spend ratio against 3 with an IF.

title: This channel's CPA target
context: The Channels table (K2:N7) holds each channel's target CPA.
task: Look up the target CPA for the channel used in the week in row 2.
hint: Match the channel name into the Channels table; work out which column the target CPA sits in.

title: CAMP03 budget
context: The Campaigns table (P2:U9) lists each campaign's budget.
task: Look up the budget assigned to campaign CAMP03.
hint: Match the campaign ID into the Campaigns table and pull back its budget column.

title: Week of the year
context: Reporting groups rows by which week of the year they fall in.
task: Roughly which week number of the year does the week-start date in row 2 fall in? (Count the days into the year and convert to whole weeks.)
hint: Find how many days into the year the date is, divide by 7 and round up.

title: Month of the week
context: Monthly rollups need the month number.
task: What month number (1-12) does the week in row 2 start in?
hint: Extract the month from the week-start date.

title: Short week label
context: Charts label each week like "07 Apr".
task: Show the week-start date in row 2 formatted like "07 Apr".
hint: Use a text function with a day-and-month date pattern.

title: Campaign length
context: The Campaigns table stores each campaign's start and end date; count both endpoints.
task: How many days long is the campaign in row 2 of the Campaigns table, counting both the first and last day?
hint: Subtract the start date from the end date, then add one.

title: Channel initial
context: A compact chart tag uses just the first letter of the channel.
task: Return the first letter of the channel name for the week in row 2.
hint: A text function that takes characters from the left.

title: Campaign URL slug
context: URLs use a lower-case, hyphenated version of the campaign name (e.g. Spring Sale becomes spring-sale).
task: Turn the campaign name in row 2 of the Campaigns table into a slug: lower case with spaces replaced by hyphens.
hint: Replace spaces with hyphens, then force lower case.

title: Spend in thousands
context: A tile shows spend compactly, like "3.2K".
task: Show the spend for the week in row 2 in thousands, formatted like "3.2K".
hint: Divide spend by 1000, format to one decimal, then tack on a "K".

title: How many campaigns?
context: The Campaigns table lists each campaign by ID; the team wants the count.
task: How many campaigns are listed in the Campaigns table?
hint: Count the filled campaign-ID cells — they are text, so plain COUNT won't do.

title: Total campaign budget
context: Planning wants the combined budget across all campaigns.
task: What is the total budget across every campaign in the Campaigns table?
hint: Total the budget column of the Campaigns table.

title: Performance and profitable?
context: A flag marks weeks that were both a Performance push and profitable.
task: For the week in row 2, return TRUE only if its objective is Performance AND its revenue beat its spend.
hint: Combine two conditions that must both hold.

title: Dead week?
context: A data check flags weeks with no clicks or no conversions at all.
task: For the week in row 2, return TRUE if it had zero clicks OR zero conversions.
hint: Either condition being true is enough.

title: Meta share of spend
context: Leadership wants Meta's cut of the budget as a percentage.
task: What share of total spend went to the Meta channel? Show it formatted like 12.3%.
hint: Divide Meta's spend by total spend, then format as a percentage.

title: Weeks tracked
context: Every week has one row per channel, so total rows divided by the number of channels gives the weeks covered.
task: How many distinct weeks does the data cover, given each channel appears once per week?
hint: Divide the count of week-start values by the number of channels in the Channels table.
